quick: Empty stomach; AVOID milk, dairy and calcium (chelation)
Not indicated (men); estrogenic - avoid in women/pregnancy
Limit; potential hepatic and GI irritation
Thromboembolism, BP, glucose, LFTs, fluid retention, calcium
summary: Estramustine phosphate is an oral conjugate of estradiol and a nitrogen mustard (normustine) used for palliative treatment of metastatic and/or progressive prostate cancer. The usual dose is 14 mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses, taken on an empty stomach while avoiding milk, dairy products and calcium-rich foods or supplements, which chelate the drug and reduce absorption. Because of its estrogenic component, the major risks are thromboembolism (DVT, PE, stroke, MI), fluid retention and gynecomastia.
indications: Palliative treatment of metastatic and/or progressive carcinoma of the prostate

dosage.d: 14 mg/kg of body weight per day (approx 10-16 mg/kg/day) in 3 or 4 divided doses
dosage.n: Most patients treated in the 14 mg/kg/day range; take with water on empty stomach

dosage.d: Continue as long as favorable response; assess at 30-90 days
dosage.n: Discontinue if no objective improvement after adequate trial

admin: Take each dose with water at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals (empty stomach)
AVOID taking with milk, milk products, or calcium-rich foods/antacids - calcium chelates estramustine and impairs absorption
Store capsules refrigerated (2-8 C) per label
Maintain consistent dosing schedule of 3-4 divided doses daily
moa: Estramustine phosphate is dephosphorylated to estramustine and estromustine. These metabolites bind microtubule-associated proteins (MAPs) and tubulin, causing disassembly of microtubules and arresting cells in metaphase (antimitotic, antimicrotubule action). The estradiol portion also exerts antigonadotropic/estrogenic effects that suppress testosterone. The original concept of nitrogen-mustard alkylation contributes little; cytotoxicity is mainly antimicrotubule.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to estradiol or to nitrogen mustard
Active thrombophlebitis or thromboembolic disorders (unless the tumor itself is the cause and benefit outweighs risk)
relative: History of thromboembolic disease, MI, stroke or coronary disease
Poorly controlled congestive heart failure or edema
monitor: Conditions worsened by fluid retention (epilepsy, migraine, renal dysfunction)

preg: Estramustine is used to treat men and is not indicated in women. The estrogenic component can cause fetal harm; it should not be used in pregnancy or by women of childbearing potential.
lact: Not applicable - the drug is indicated only for men with prostate cancer.
renal: Specific renal dose adjustments are not established; use with caution in renal impairment and monitor for fluid retention and worsening function.
hepatic: Estramustine is metabolized and excreted partly through the liver; use with caution and avoid in patients with significantly impaired hepatic function. Monitor liver function tests, which may become abnormal and usually normalize after stopping.

major: Drugs increasing thromboembolic risk - additive risk of DVT/PE/stroke; monitor closely
moderate: Milk, dairy products, calcium-containing antacids or supplements - chelate estramustine and markedly reduce absorption; separate or avoid
Other estrogens / hormonal agents - additive estrogenic effects
minor: ACE inhibitors - increased risk of angioedema reported with estramustine
interactions.food: Milk, dairy and calcium-rich foods or supplements form an insoluble chelate that reduces estramustine absorption - take on an empty stomach and avoid concurrent calcium.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; may add to gastrointestinal irritation and hepatic burden.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise glucose, alter LFTs, lower phosphate, and (estrogen effect) decrease testosterone; can affect thyroid, cortisol-binding and other binding-globulin assays.

monitoring: Signs and symptoms of thromboembolism (leg swelling/pain, chest pain, dyspnea, neurologic deficit)
Fluid retention, weight and cardiac status; serum calcium in bone metastases
counsel: Take on an empty stomach and avoid milk, cheese, yogurt, calcium tablets or antacids around dosing
This medicine increases the risk of blood clots - report leg swelling/pain, sudden chest pain, breathlessness, weakness or trouble speaking immediately
Breast enlargement/tenderness and reduced sexual function can occur
Keep capsules in the refrigerator; report swelling, rapid weight gain or yellowing of the skin/eyes
pk: Antitumor response assessed over weeks; estrogenic effects early
Estramustine/estromustine peak within hours of dosing
pearls: Major risk is thromboembolism (DVT, PE, MI, stroke) from the estradiol component - counsel and monitor for clot symptoms
Take on an empty stomach and avoid milk/dairy/calcium - calcium chelation can drastically lower absorption
Acts mainly as an antimicrotubule agent, not primarily as an alkylator despite the nitrogen-mustard structure
Combination with ACE inhibitors raises angioedema risk; watch for facial/laryngeal swelling
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip it. Do not double the dose. Resume the regular 3-4 times daily schedule.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. In overdose, monitor hematologic and hepatic parameters for at least 6 weeks and give supportive care; manage thromboembolic and cardiovascular complications as they arise.
